summary: Oregon's westernmost and oldest standing lighthouse, a brick tower lit on 20 December 1870 and kept for decades by James Langlois and James Hughes.

access.note: Tower closed to tours since 2020 for structural repairs; exterior viewable; greeting center in Cape Blanco State Park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record gives 1870 built and first lit 1870; sources agree the tower was completed in 1870 and first lit on 20 December 1870.

Record says the original lens was order 1 and the lens now in place is order 2. Sources agree: first-order original (Lighthouse Friends, 1914 Bulletin), second-order Henry-Lepaute lens installed 1936. The NRHP nomination muddles the two by giving the second-order dimensions for the original.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in text: Langlois's dates (USLHS head keeper 1885-1919 with acting 1883-85; LF 1883-1919; NRHP 1883-1912, arrival 1875 vs USLHS 1876; the 1910 newspaper OCR gives 12 August of a garbled year, possibly 1877); brick counts (8,000 vs 80,000); lens order of the original; Alaskan casualties (NRHP 31 of 47 vs 1889 newspaper: crew only, 34, five first reported drowned); South Portland dead (18 vs 21); Chanslor survivors (NRHP 3 crew, Heritage Society 3 of 39 'passengers', 1919 paper 3 known rescued of 40); automation 1980 vs 1979. Record characteristic Fl W 10s differs from NRHP/Bulletin 20 s pattern; not checked against the current Light List. NRHP says Terry became keeper in 1874; USLHS lists Charles W. Tracey 1874 then Charles H. Peirce 1874-83; not reconciled and neither is named in prose. 1869 Light-House Board report is cited only second-hand (via the NRHP and Lighthouse Friends), since the corpus holds no volume before 1891. Fiscal-year note: the 1893 report entry states December 1892 explicitly. Corpus page numbers for the 1900 and 1893 reports are scan pages (printed page not verified). Heritage Society page 'lightstation.html' and 'lightstation-history.html' differ in details (five records vs at least five). The Cape Blanco Heritage Society website also holds Hughes House info; the Hughes House itself (separate NRHP listing) is not covered here. Roster is from the USLHS archive; post-1948 USCG names listed as the archive prints them. Hughes appears twice in the roster as second then first assistant. Checker 2026-10-27: Port Orford distance is stated as nomination 6 miles vs Lighthouse Friends 9 (Heritage/SF Call give other figures); duplex distance 100 ft (NRHP) vs 125 ft (LF); the nomination's own lens dimensions are internally inconsistent (6'8 x 4'8 vs 6'1 x 4'7), so the story gives no figures. The nomination's NRHP number is not printed in the PDF; footnote 1 calls it the NPGallery document number.
